questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can make it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: Why is riding directly beside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start riding.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean.
You may have less traction as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Your tires are already using some traction to turn while leaning, so less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen in the dark.
They involve inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrians crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing ahead.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder.
Ride under the speed limit.
Wear a helmet.
Do not carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best thing you can do to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: How often should you check that your headlight and taillight work?

options.text: Once a month.
Once a week.
Before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always test your lights before you start riding. Working lights are essential to your safety every time you ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves on rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving on rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. If you feel weaving, simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to fight the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?

options.text: A DOT-compliant helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects against injuries. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors like red, orange, yellow, and green make you more visible. Dark colors like black are harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you of upcoming conditions. This sign tells you that traffic will merge onto the road from the right.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do about your lane position?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single part of the lane you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed to use when exiting a highway. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and weaker than car headlights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without coming to a complete stop.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely. Look for pedestrians and other vehicles crossing before you go.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Maintain your usual space cushion.
Brake later than usual.
Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. You should ride slower, especially in curves and over bumps. The extra weight also makes speeding up, slowing down, and stopping take longer, so keep more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: How do you brake hardest in a straight line?

options.text: Using the front brake, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake, then the front brake.
Using the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using the front and rear brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time for maximum stopping power. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks, release the brake pressure. Then slowly apply the brake again with gentle pressure.

questions.question: When your front tire goes flat, your steering will feel:

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Modify the exhaust system.
Clean and adjust your mirrors.
Clean your wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean and adjust your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, make sure your mirrors are clean and adjusted properly. Your mirrors should show the road behind you and to the side of you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep going straight. Gradually brake only on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after finishing a turn or lane change. Leaving your signal on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is on top and green is on bottom. On a horizontal light, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to be more visible at intersections. Position yourself in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can provide protection in the event of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can provide protection in the event of a crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap but loose enough that you can move easily.

questions.question: What are the colors of signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Direction signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
Always be in the left lane to be the farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight has a better chance of being spotted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the portion of the lane that will bring you into other drivers' fields of vision at the earliest possible moment.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane where oncoming drivers will see you as early as possible. For example, at a blind corner on your right, ride on the left side of your lane so you are visible sooner.
